steps: Map your review route by site section with your content owners: who writes, who checks legal or safety wording, who approves, and who covers urgent corrections out of hours.
Remove the replicate right from your author groups, so Sites console publishes become requests, and customize the request workflow with review, legal or safety sign-off and approval steps.
Assign each step to a group, since a single user's work item cannot be delegated, and add an urgent route your on-call approvers can complete out of hours.
Keep the workflows non-transient so their history is saved, create a page version at each publish, keep both for your retention period, and test every route with your reviewers.
deliverables: Customized request workflow with an urgent route
Publish permissions for author and approver groups
Approval route map by site section
Approval record kept for your retention period
Route test results, signed off by your reviewers
asks: Your content owners and reviewers, with the sections and the legal or safety wording each approves
An out-of-hours rota of approvers, and how each one is reached
How long you must keep approval records, and who will check them
risk: A page going live unreviewed: we remove the authors' right to publish, so every change, urgent corrections included, passes an approver and leaves a record.
outcome: Every page change is approved before it goes live, urgent corrections included, and each published version can be traced to its approval.

steps: Map each country site to its language master with your central and market teams, and agree which components each market may correct locally.
Integrate your translation service provider with AEM, run the first translation projects, then change one source page, send it again and review the updated translation in its launch.
Deploy the blueprint configuration through the CI/CD pipeline, create each country site as an MSM Live Copy of its language master, and set the agreed rollout configurations.
Test one shared page per market with its author: break inheritance on a corrected component, roll out a central update, and check the correction stays while other components update.
deliverables: Country sites as MSM Live Copies of language masters
Translation provider integration and first translation projects
Blueprint and rollout configurations
Local correction rules and test results by market
asks: Your translation service provider's contact and account details, and the languages they cover for you
A central content owner and one author per market who agree what may be corrected locally
The markets, the languages each one serves and the shared pages to test with
risk: A local correction that also stops later central changes reaching that component: we keep a register of every broken inheritance and review it with each market after central updates.
outcome: Each country site takes central updates in its own language by rollout, and the corrections your market teams make locally stay in place.

steps: Agree with your product data owner the fields the public site may show, leaving out prices, stock and customer terms, plus the approved values each file must match.
Build a Content Fragment Model with only those fields, and show each product's fragment on its product page with the Content Fragment Component.
Build an App Builder application that a cron job runs each night, dropping unlisted fields and writing each passing file to AEM Author through the Content Fragment Management API.
Hold a late, incomplete or conflicting file with the published values left live, report each run to your product data owner, who publishes from the console, and test each case.
deliverables: Signed-off field list and file checks
Content Fragment Model and product page display
Nightly import in App Builder
Test results, including a file with prices and stock
Runbook for publishing, held files and alerts
asks: A sample nightly file, its field list and the time it usually arrives
A product data owner who approves the field list and decides on held files
A file location your team provides that the nightly import can read
risk: A wrong or private value reaching a product page: only listed fields are written, and a file that fails a check changes nothing until your product data owner decides.
outcome: Each night your checked ERP or PIM specifications reach AEM for your product data owner to publish, with prices and stock never written and every held file reported.

steps: Inventory every page and file on your current site with its traffic and inbound links, and agree with your content owners which to retain, merge or retire.
Map each content type to the template and components its pages will use, and write the import scripts that build the pages from that map.
Test the import on each content type with your authors, then load the retained pages in small content packages through Package Manager and their images and files through Bulk Import.
Build the redirect map for every retired, merged or moved URL, load it as a pipeline-free rewrite map or as Dispatcher or CDN redirect rules, and test every entry.
Run the final import after the content freeze and publish it, then check sampled pages against the source, crawl for broken links and test the inventory's inbound links.
deliverables: Page inventory with retain, merge and retire decisions
Content mapping and import scripts
Published pages, images and files in AEM Sites
Tested redirect map
Content, link and redirect check report
asks: Export access to your current CMS, plus your site analytics and inbound link data
Content owners who decide which pages to retain, merge or retire, and review samples
A content freeze window agreed with your authors before the final import
risk: Pages or links lost in the move: every page is counted against the inventory, and every retired, merged or moved URL is redirected and tested before launch.
outcome: Your retained pages are in AEM Sites on their agreed templates, checked against the source, and every old URL and known inbound link reaches the agreed page.

steps: Agree with your document owners which documents carry an expiry date and who approves replacements, and write the runbook: replacements keep the document's name and folder, as new versions.
List each withdrawn document's pages on its References tab, agree each page's change with its owner, then set the Expires field and unpublish urgent withdrawals at once.
Run the first replacements with your editors: upload each as a new version, check its pages on the References tab, publish, then test a revert in the Timeline and republish.
Hide expired assets in the desktop app and Adobe Asset Link where you use them, and test with an author account that expired documents cannot be found or published.
deliverables: Document rules and editor runbook
Expiry dates on the agreed documents
First replacements, published and checked page by page
Test results for expiry, hiding and revert
asks: A document owner who approves each replacement and each withdrawal
The list of documents to withdraw or limit in time, with their end dates
A few editors for the first replacements and the tests
risk: A document withdrawn while pages still link to it: we list those pages on its References tab first, and each owner agrees the page's change before the expiry date.
outcome: Each approved replacement is published as a new version once its pages are checked, a wrong one can be reverted and republished, and expired documents leave your public site.

steps: Inventory your active email programs, subscription types and suppression records, and agree with your legal team which choice wins when sources or the CRM conflict, such as the most restrictive.
Create a custom field for each subscription type and the subscription center, then import your people and their choices, checking a sample file against the export first.
Set Unsubscribed, Marketing Suspended or Blocklisted with Change Data Value flow steps on every record holding a suppressed address, and mark old hard bounces as Email Invalid.
Rebuild your active programs with no marketing email set as operational, and before the first migrated send, check its blocked people and that its recipients include no suppressed address.
deliverables: Program, preference and suppression inventory
Conflict rule and decision log
People, choices and suppression flags in Marketo Engage
Subscription center and rebuilt active programs
Pre-send check record for the first migrated campaign
asks: Exports of your people, subscription choices and suppression records from your current platform
A decision from your legal team on the rule for conflicting preferences
The active email programs to rebuild, with an owner who approves each one
risk: A person who opted out receiving a migrated email: we first send to internal test records, some set as Unsubscribed or Blocklisted, and confirm those receive nothing.
outcome: Your active programs run in Marketo Engage, with every subscription choice carried across and every suppressed person blocked from marketing email.
